Solution: If g(x)<=f(x)<=h(x) for all sufficiently close domain inputs other than the target, and both bounding functions tend to the same finite L, then f(x)->L. Question Choices: Evaluate lim x->0 of sin(x)/x. Use radians.
Hints: This is the fundamental trigonometric limit.|Angles are in radians.
Solution: In radians, sin(u)/u tends to 1 as u->0. For nonzero constants a,b, rewrite sin(ax)/(bx)=(a/b)[sin(ax)/(ax)], so its limit is a/b. Degree-valued inputs introduce the conversion factor pi/180; they do not give the same standard limit 1. lim x->0 of sin(x)/x = 1
